changes.summary: A preliminary Los Angeles County review reported substantial registration-status, voting-history and citizenship mismatches in a 200-name sample from the federal list.
changes.duplicate_review: Updated the existing election-enforcement lifecycle. The federal California list, county demands and litigation already map to NAT-2026-09-15-003; no new canonical count was created.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Associated Press reported from a Los Angeles County court filing that a preliminary review of 200 names from the federal 20,000-person California list found more than 40% had canceled registrations, more than 70% had no voting history and nearly 40% were born in the United States. AP also reported that Mendocino County received names of people who were not county residents. DOJ spokeswoman Kiersten Pels said the department was not requesting a purge, registration cancellation or programmatic action and instead sought cooperation; a Ninth Circuit panel was scheduled to hear the compliance dispute on October 25.
source_inspections.hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact normalized evidence extract retained here, not a claim of hashing the publisher's complete webpage.
